sources.title: National Underground Asset Register (NUAR)
sources.publisher: Government Digital Service / DSIT / Geospatial Commission
sources.verified_claim: NUAR is a digital map of underground pipes and cables using data from over 600 public and private asset owners; exact candidate assets still require an authorised site query.

sources.title: Government Digital Service - About us
sources.verified_claim: GDS identifies continued NUAR rollout as part of its current geospatial and digital-infrastructure responsibilities.

sources.title: National underground asset register - planning consideration
sources.verified_claim: Planning Data records NUAR as a potential planning consideration/use case; the design-stage record does not expose a candidate asset intersection.

sources.title: National Underground Asset Register
sources.verified_claim: GLA describes the London NUAR platform combining buried water, sewer, gas, electricity and telecoms assets for participating users; it is not a public parcel search.

sources.title: National Underground Asset Register minimum viable product
sources.verified_claim: The MVP includes safe-dig functionality and London coverage, but historic rollout status is retained rather than assumed to represent a current candidate query.

sources.title: National Underground Asset Register project update - November 2024
sources.publisher: Government Digital Service / DSIT / Geospatial Commission
sources.verified_claim: The project update records service transition and operating-model milestones; programme progress is not candidate utility clearance.

sources.title: OS named future operator of National Underground Asset Register
sources.verified_claim: Ordnance Survey was named future operator; operator status does not change the need for authorised, location-specific asset data.

sources.title: National Underground Asset Register: unlocking value for industry and the wider economy
sources.verified_claim: The economic case explains benefits of centralised underground-asset data access; economic benefits are not parcel utility-capacity evidence.
